chunks: And by this chain of narration: from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-'Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Ibrahim ibn 'Umar al-Yamani, from Abu Khalid al-Qammat,
that he heard Abu 'Abd Allah (AS) speaking about water that a man passes by, which is a stagnant pool containing a putrid dead carcass —

Abu 'Abd Allah (AS) said: «If the water's smell or taste has changed, do not drink from it and do not perform wudu with it; and if neither its smell nor its taste has changed, then drink and perform wudu.»
As for what indicates the [minimum] quantity of kurr [water] —

key_terms.الْكُرِّ: kurr — the minimum volume of water in Shia jurisprudence that resists impurity by contact
key_terms.نَقِيعٌ: stagnant pool, body of standing water

ai.seo_question: According to Imam al-Sadiq (AS), when does water containing a dead animal become impure and forbidden for drinking or wudu?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS), transmitted through Abu Khalid al-Qammat, establishes the jurisprudential ruling on stagnant water containing a putrid animal carcass. The Imam rules that if the water's smell or taste has changed, both drinking and wudu are forbidden; if neither has changed, both are permissible. The text concludes with the author's (Sheikh al-Tusi's) transitional note introducing the next section on the minimum volume of kurr water.
